Article Title: 'Didn't want Mamata to contest another election': Suvendu Adhikari on why he kept Bhabanipur seat
Article Text:
शुभेंदु अधिकारी और ममता बनर्जी

NEW DELHI: Explaining his decision to vacate his Nandigram stronghold and retain Bhabanipur, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday that vacating the Bhabanipur seat would have given his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee , another opportunity to contest the subsequent bypoll and return to the state assembly.Adhikari, who won both seats in the West Bengal assembly elections in April, defeated Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur. He had also defeated the then chief minister in Nandigram in the 2021 assembly elections, following which the TMC supremo contested a bypoll from Bhabanipur and won.The chief minister also took a dig at his predecessor, suggesting that she should retire from electoral politics given her age.“Had I vacated Bhabanipur, the person (Mamata Banerjee) I had defeated twice would have got another opportunity to contest an election. I did not want to give her that opportunity. I had trounced her in Bhabanipur, and I would urge her not to contest elections any more. You have already crossed 75 years of age. There is no need to enter the electoral fray any further. You should take rest at home,” PTI quoted Adhikari as saying.He made the remarks after Hasirani Rath and Shakharav Sarkar were sworn in as BJP MLAs following their victories in the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls earlier this month.The BJP leader also sought to reassure people in Nandigram, who he said were “upset” with him for leaving the constituency. He asserted that he would fulfil his commitments to them through Hasirani Rath, the newly elected MLA from Nandigram.“The people of Nandigram were upset with me for leaving the constituency, but I have explained my decision to them. I had to leave Nandigram for this reason. The people have now elected Hasirani Rath with a margin of 1.22 lakh votes. I will fulfil my promise to them through her,” he added.Hasirani Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, Adhikari’s aide who was shot dead on May 6, two days after the West Bengal assembly election results were declared. The BJP came to power in the state for the first time, ending the TMC’s 15-year rule.Turning to the murder of Chandranath Rath, Adhikari alleged that his aide was killed because of his association with him, describing it as a “supari”, or contract killing.“Chandranath was murdered simply because he was my aide. The CBI has arrested seven people, including the shooters and contract killers. What remains to be established is where the Rs 2 crore ‘supari’ for the contract killing came from. Was it Camac Street, Kalighat or Diamond Harbour? Once that is known, the investigation will be complete,” he said.Adhikari appeared to be referring to Camac Street, associated with the office of Trinamool Congress national general secretary and Mamata's nephew Abhishek Banerjee; Kalighat, where Mamata Banerjee resides; and Diamond Harbour, the Lok Sabha constituency represented by Abhishek Banerjee.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said vacating the Bhabanipur seat would have given his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee, another opportunity to contest the subsequent bypoll and return to the state assembly. He made the remarks after Hasirani Rath and Shakharav Sarkar were sworn in as BJP MLAs.

Article Title: BJP fields Hardeep Singh Puri as its candidate for Rajya Sabha bypoll from MP

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party BJP ) on Wednesday nominated senior leader and Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri for the Rajya Sabha bypoll in Madhya Pradesh.According to an official press release issued from the BJP's central office on Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg, the party's Central Election Committee cleared Puri's name for the Upper House seat."The Central Election Committee of the Bharatiya Janata Party has given its approval to the name for the upcoming Rajya Sabha bye-election 2026 in Madhya Pradesh: Hardeep Singh Puri," the statement read.The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of former Union minister L Murugan, who vacated the seat on October 14. His term in the Rajya Sabha was originally scheduled to end on April 2, 2030.The Election Commission announced the schedule for the bypoll on October 22.According to the schedule, the notification for the election will be issued on October 26. The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny will take place on November 3. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until November 5.Polling will be held on November 12 from 9am to 4pm, followed by counting at 5pm on the same day. The entire election process is scheduled to be completed by November 16, the poll panel said.Puri, a former diplomat who later entered politics, currently serves as a Union Cabinet minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's government and holds the petroleum and natural gas portfolio.
Article Summary: Hardeep Singh Puri is a Union Cabinet minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government. The bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of former Union minister L Murugan, who vacated the seat on October 14. His term in the Rajya Sabha was originally scheduled to end on April 2, 2030.

Article Title: 'Failed to establish presence': BJP takes 'ballot paper' jibe at Rahul after Congress draws blank in MLC polls
Article Text:
BJP targets Rahul after MLC poll results, says Congress failed to make its presence felt

Karnataka: BJP-JD(S) sweep all four seats

Uttar Pradesh: BJP vs SP battle

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Wednesday targeted Congress over the results of MLC elections across four states, claiming that the grand old party has "failed to make its presence felt" in the polls conducted using ballot papers.The BJP's strong remarks came amid Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's repeated allegations against the Election Commission and CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities.Addressing a presser, BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi said, "The message is clear... the Congress party has failed to make its presence felt in these (MLC ) elections. More importantly, these elections were conducted using ballot boxes and ballot papers, yet the Congress failed to establish its presence. To put it in terms that the Congress leaders would understand better, the party has failed to make its very existence felt. This makes it clear that the Congress party lacks the ability to secure public support or the support of the voters concerned in any election, whether it is conducted using EVMs or ballot papers."BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi launched attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi as the BJP and its NDA allies registered wins in the MLC elections.He said, "The Congress party should understand that Rahul Gandhi, after spending nearly two weeks sightseeing and enjoying himself, has now returned to the limelight and is talking about launching a movement that could create problems for the Indian economy. He must understand that neither the public nor the MLAs are with him. The Congress party must understand that public support is earned through hard work, not through sightseeing and leisure trips.""Our national president, Nitin Nabin, is travelling to Uttar Pradesh, while Amit Shah is in Punjab. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi had disappeared from the scene and was wandering around 'Champa'. 'Champa' was the ancient name of Vietnam. After that, he expects to receive public support. I would therefore like to tell the Congress party... give up your habit of avoiding hard work, and the slogan of 'vote theft' will automatically disappear," Sudhanshu Trivedi added.The BJP's remarks came as the party and its allies registered wins in several Legislative Council constituencies, while the Congress faced setbacks in Karnataka and Bihar.In Karnataka, the BJP took a jibe at chief minister DK Shivakumar after the opposition BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four seats in the state's Legislative Council elections, leaving the ruling Congress without a win.The BJP's Karnataka unit posted on X, saying, "DK, it’s done, bro!"It added, "NDA SWEEPS 4/4 Teachers’ and Graduates’ constituencies in the MLC elections!"The BJP retained the North-East Teachers', South-East Graduates' and West Graduates' constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers' seat from the Congress.In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins in Varanasi and Agra, while the BJP secured three of the 11 Legislative Council seats, with counting under way in the remaining constituencies, officials said on Wednesday.SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP of resorting to alleged electoral malpractice to win the Uttar Pradesh MLC elections. He claimed that irregularities in the counting process had exposed a conspiracy to defeat SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi.In a post on X, Akhilesh alleged that BJP leaders, their associates and officials had colluded to manipulate the counting process. He claimed that the alleged treatment of Tripathi had angered teachers and his community, and vowed that his party would oppose what he described as injustice and harassment.The BJP has denied no specific allegations in the information provided.In Bihar, the Prashant Kishor-led Jan Suraaj Party opened its account in the Legislative Council elections after its candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha by 324 votes in the Darbhanga Teachers' constituency, officials said on Wednesday.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh had on Tuesday defeated his nearest rival, Independent nominee Bhushan Kumar Jha, to win the Tirhut Teachers' constituency.Counting was still under way for some Legislative Council seats, officials said.
Article Summary: BJP targets Rahul after MLC poll results, says Congress failed to make its presence felt. BJP-JD(S) sweep all four seats in Karnataka. Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins in Varanasi and Agra. BJP secured three of the 11 Legislative Council seats.

Article Title: UP MLC polls: SP secures Varanasi and Agra seat, BJP wins 4
Article Text:
Lal Bihari Yadav secured the Varanasi Teachers' seat





LUCKNOW: BJP retained four Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, including both constituencies in Meerut, the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat and the Lucknow Teachers’ seat, while the Samajwadi Party secured victories in the Varanasi and Agra Teachers’ constituencies as counting for 11 MLC seats continued.In the Meerut-Saharanpur Graduates’ constituency, BJP’s sitting MLC Dinesh Goyal retained his seat, defeating SP candidate Pramod Singh Bhati by 12,855 votes. BJP’s Shrichand Sharma also retained the Meerut Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Nitin Tomar by 13,241 votes.BJP’s Hari Singh Dhillon retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Haji Mohammad Danish Akhtar.In another victory for the BJP, sitting MLC Umesh Dwivedi retained the Lucknow Teachers’ constituency, defeating SP candidate Sushil Kumar (Baba). UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary congratulated Dwivedi on his victory in a post on X on Wednesday morning, expressing confidence that he would continue working for the development of the education sector.Meanwhile, SP’s sitting MLC Lal Bihari Yadav retained the Varanasi Teachers’ constituency, defeating BJP candidate Pramod Mishra by approximately 4,900 votes.In the Agra Teachers’ constituency, SP candidate Akash Agrawal emerged victorious, defeating BJP candidate Hari Kishore Tiwari. Agrawal had won the same seat as an Independent in 2020. His latest victory means he has retained the constituency, this time as an SP candidate.In the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, BJP’s Dhruv Tripathi was leading by a narrow margin of 110 votes in the last available update, with Independent candidate Rajeev Yadav and SP candidate Sanjayan also in contention.Polling for five Graduates’ and six Teachers’ constituencies was held on October 23, with 152 candidates in the fray. Repolling at three polling stations in the Agra Teachers’ constituency took place on Monday following orders from the Election Commission.Final results from the remaining constituencies were awaited.
Article Summary: BJP retained four Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, including both constituencies in Meerut, the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat and the Lucknow Teachers' seat. Samajwadi Party secured victories in the Varanasi and Agra Teachers' constituencies.

Article Title: Omar inducts 4 ministers, dissent spills over in NC ranks

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah ’s cabinet expansion triggered open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in National Conference after four ministers were inducted Tuesday. MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi, who had expected a berth until the last moment, broke down and other legislators accused the party brass of shutting them out. Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath to Ali Mohammad Sagar, Shamima Firdous, Mir Saifullah and Altaf Ahmad Kaloo, taking the cabinet’s strength to nine, including Omar. He dropped Satish Sharma, leaving only two ministers from Jammu region — deputy CM Surinder Choudhary and Javed Ahmed Rana.Legislators alleged a lack of internal democracy. “I am a law graduate, while the MLA chosen has not even passed matriculation,” Larmi said.Independent MLA Muzaffar Iqbal Khan, who supports NC, boycotted the ceremony, alleging discrimination against Poonch-Rajouri. Khan plans to convene six independent MLAs supporting NC-led govt to discuss their next move.Supporters of MLA Mubarak Gul protested at the party headquarters, while Nazir Ahmad Khan was said to be unhappy with the expansion. Health minister Sakina Itoo dismissed the protests.The 90-member assembly allows a maximum of nine ministers, including the CM. Omar was sworn in on Oct 16, 2024, with five ministers. Three berths remained vacant for nearly two years.An NC legislator said the next three months would test whether the party brass could contain the anger. “The way the expansion was carried out has humiliated party legislators. There seems to be no democracy within the party,” he said.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah ’s cabinet expansion triggered open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in National Conference. MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi, who had expected a berth until the last moment, broke down and other legislators accused the party brass of shutting them out.Independent MLA Muzaffar Iqbal Khan, who supports NC, boycotted the ceremony, alleging discrimination against Poonch-Rajouri.

Article Title: Karnataka MLC polls: Big setback for DK Shivakumar as BJP-led NDA wins all 4 seats
Article Text: BENGALURU: In a major setback to the ruling Congress and chief minister D K Shivakumar, the BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23, sweeping both teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies.The NDA fielded three BJP candidates and one JD(S) candidate.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated Congress veteran and five-time MLC Puttanna in the Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency, while BJP candidate Shashil G Namoshi registered his fifth victory in the North-East Teachers’ constituency, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur by 3,297 votes. Namoshi secured 15,596 first-preference votes against Mattur’s 12,299.Counting concluded at Kalaburagi, where around 30,253 voters had exercised their franchise. Of the votes counted, 28,380 were valid, while 1,873 were rejected.In the graduates’ constituencies, BJP candidates SV Sankanur and KM Suresh also emerged victorious, completing the NDA’s clean sweep of all four seats.In the West Graduates’ constituency, Sankanur secured his third consecutive victory, defeating Congress rival Mohan Limbikai.In the other graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate KM Suresh won the seat, ensuring that the NDA did not concede any ground to the ruling party in the elections.This is the second biennial legislative council election since Shivakumar became chief minister on June 3. In the June 18 elections to seven council seats from the MLAs’ quota, Congress won five seats and the BJP secured two. However, the ruling party failed to replicate that performance in the teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies.Ranganath won the Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency on his third attempt, defeating Puttanna by 908 votes. He secured 10,810 first-preference votes against Puttanna’s 9,902.Ranganath had lost to Puttanna in the 2022 and 2024 elections. This time, he capitalised on a sympathy wave to secure victory. Puttanna had contested as a BJP candidate in 2022 before switching to Congress for the 2024 by-election.
Article Summary: The BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23. The NDA fielded three BJP candidates and one JD(S) candidate. This is the second biennial legislative council election since Shivakumar became chief minister on June 3.

Article Title: Congress slams EC affidavit, terms it ‘deceptive, deceitful & duplicitous’

NEW DELHI: Dubbing the Election Commission’s affidavit in Supreme Court as “deceptive, deceitful and duplicitous”, Congress Tuesday said CEC Gyanesh Kumar has been taking unilateral decisions and the EC’s claims on Form 6 are contradictory.Taking to X, Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh wrote, “Oh what a tangled web we weave, when first we practice to deceive.” He said that as per the EC’s claims, major SIR orders were formally approved by all three ECs.“But two election commissioners objected on record to grave violations and illegal actions taking place on orders of CEC — their objections were disregarded. The commissioners were not even informed and learnt of these decisions from the news.This is not unanimity but unilateral decision-making,” he said.Ramesh said EC’s stand on “illegal amendment to Form 6” is deceptive as it first claimed SC had approved the new declaration attached to Form 6 but changed its tune after SC contradicted its claim. “It now claims the new declaration form is separate, and Form 6 was not amended. But this is a deception — Form 6 could not be submitted online without filling this mandatory declaration,” he said.He said the EC has been silent on illegal centralisation of rolls through ECINET by overriding electoral registration officers who are the statutory authority — which was put on record by the commissioners.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday said that the INDIA bloc's "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be held at party president Mallikarjun Kharge 's residence.This comes after Congress accused the government of denying permission for the event at the state-run Ashoka Hotel.Earlier in the day, Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal said the hotel had initially allowed the event to be held on its premises but later denied permission following police intervention."How many permissions will you deny, Mr Amit Shah? Article Title: 'We know everything': SC on pleas alleging unilateral decisions by CEC, gives petitioners 10 days to reply
Article Text:
The three-judge bench adjourned the hearing to November 17.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that it would examine all aspects of the Election Commission of India 's (ECI) decision-making process amid allegations that key decisions, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken without the unanimous consent."We know everything. We will examine," Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said while hearing a batch of petitions challenging the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the poll panel, Live Law reported.The three-judge bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, adjourned the hearing to November 17.The top court granted the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the ECI’s counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday and asserted that the decisions in question were unanimous.The CJI's remark came after senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for leader of opposition on Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, urged the court to direct the ECI to preserve file notings and internal communications related to its decisions.Singhvi argued that the records were crucial to determining whether the decisions concerning the SIR were taken unanimously or unilaterally."This whole issue depends on the decision-making process, consultation, and whether the decision was unanimous or not unanimous.Let file notings, etc be preserved," Singhvi added.The petitions challenge the functioning of Gyanesh Kumar alleged that several ECI decisions, including those related to the SIR, were issued without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners.The bench also issued notices to the ECI and other respondents on a fresh petition filed by Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen. The plea alleges that changes were made to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR without the Supreme Court’s approval.Senior advocate and MP Maneka Guruswamy, appearing for Sen, told the court that the poll panel had wrongly claimed that the changes to Form 6 were approved by the top court.The CJI said the court would examine all the issues and asked senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the first petitioner, Rakesh Kumar Singh to file a rejoinder within 10 days to the ECI’s reply affidavit.Earlier on Monday, in its 248-page affidavit, the ECI strongly defended the SIR and rejected allegations that Form 6, the statutory form used for voter registration, had been amended."The attempt to make aspersions against the Election Commission is unfortunate," the affidavit, filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu on behalf of the ECI said, PTI reported.The poll panel also maintained that no changes had been made to the statutory Form 6. It said the affidavit itself had been approved for filing through a unanimous decision of all three Election Commissioners.The petitions followed a report published by The Indian Express on September 25, which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the preceding 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR.According to the report, the two commissioners had objected that the decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The allegations triggered protests by opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which demanded the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The Supreme Court will take up the matter again on November 17, after the petitioners file their rejoinders to the ECI's affidavit.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that it would examine all aspects of the Election Commission of India's decision-making process. The top court granted the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the ECI’s counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday and asserted that the decisions in question were unanimous.

NEW DELHI: The Congress’ Keralam unit has tendered an unconditional apology for a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, stating that the call for his “resignation” was "inappropriate" and should not have been made on an official party platform.Sunny Joseph, president of the Keralam Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC), apologised on behalf of the state unit in response to a legal notice issued by Meenesh Dubey, joint secretary of SCBA.Joseph said in his reply to the notice, “The KPCC unequivocally reaffirms its respect for the Constitution, the independence of the judiciary and the constitutional office of the Chief Justice of India. The expressions reproduced in your notice do not represent the policy or authorised position of the KPCC and that of the Indian National Congress.”“The KPCC expressly had repudiated and withdrawn the statements reproduced in your notice. On its behalf, I tender an unconditional apology to the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India,” the statement read.Joseph noted that the person responsible for the post had published it without the approval or prior knowledge of the KPCC leadership and had since been removed from the position. He clarified, however, that his apology was on behalf of the Keralam Congress unit alone.The individual has also been asked to issue a public apology, he added.On October 12, the KPCC posted a message on X targeting the CJI, saying: “Dear Surya Kant, If law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it.”The post, which was deleted within hours following widespread criticism, followed the CJI’s remarks while hearing a plea concerning unprecedented restrictions in Delhi amid protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: The Congress’ Keralam unit has tendered an unconditional apology for a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. The call for his “resignation’ was "inappropriate" and should not have been made on an official party platform.

Article Title: Government working on bill to curb child & revenge porn: Solicitor general in SC

NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday informed Supreme Court it is in the process of drafting a bill to prevent social media circulation of child pornography, vindictive uploading of videos of consensual sexual acts after souring of relations, morphing of videos to ridicule or defame personalities, and permitting any person to file police complaint against such offensive contents.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that deliberations are on for legislative intervention to prevent circulation of sexual contents, child porn and morphed videos on social media.Mehta said he is not opposing the two PILs, one by Uday Mahurkar and another by NGO ‘Prajwala’, both of which seek robust mechanism to stop circulation of child pornography, sexual assault videos, uploading of videos of consensual adult sexual acts by jilted lovers and morphed videos.When a counsel said at present only the aggrieved person, in most cases women, can file police complaints against the person uploading such videos, the SG said the intermediary should not only be directed to immediately take down such offensive contents but also mandatorily file police complaint against the handle or digital device from which such contents were uploaded.The bench agreed that a robust legislative intervention would be required to stop the menace. It gave govt four weeks to inform the court about the outcome of the ongoing deliberations.
Article Summary: Government told the Supreme Court it is drafting a bill to prevent circulation of child pornography and offensive sexual videos online. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that deliberations are on.

Article Title: 'Cannot call anybody by that name': HC directs ex-finance secretary to mute podcast remarks against BJP MP Nishikant Dubey
Article Text:

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday directed former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg to block or mute certain allegedly objectionable remarks he made about BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on a podcast.Justice Tushar Rao Gedela noted that both Dubey and Garg were “persons of repute” and stressed that the former finance secretary should not have used an “intemperate word” during a YouTube podcast.“You cannot use a word like this. Suppose someone said ...(that to you), will you take that lightly? You cannot use the word. It is absolutely derogatory. You cannot call anybody by that name. Rest of the things, it is a debatable issue,” Justice Gedela orally observed during the hearing.Following instructions from Garg, his counsel assured the court that the retired bureaucrat would contact the podcast host to have the alleged defamatory phrases muted.However, Garg’s counsel argued that an interim injunction was unwarranted in the absence of any “aggravating circumstances”, particularly as more than a month had passed since the podcast’s release. Dubey had sought the injunction, alleging that Garg made false and malicious remarks against him during a podcast on September 17, which was subsequently published and circulated on YouTube, Facebook and other digital platforms.Before moving the Delhi high court, Dubey had issued a legal notice to Garg on September 21, demanding the immediate withdrawal and retraction of the alleged defamatory remarks, along with their removal from digital platforms.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra’s counsel also assured the court that she would remove certain related posts on X that were alleged to be defamatory.However, the lawyer maintained that Moitra would retain her right to speak on the broader issue raised in her posts.The judge issued summons to Garg and Moitra in connection with Dubey’s defamation suit, which seeks permanent and mandatory injunctions restraining them from making further allegedly defamatory remarks against him, an apology and damages of Rs 2 crore.The court also directed them to file their replies.
Article Summary: Delhi high court orders Subhash Chandra Garg to block or mute certain allegedly objectionable remarks he made about BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on a podcast. Dubey had sought the injunction, alleging that Garg made false and malicious remarks against him during a podcast on September 17.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: MLC Election Results 2026 Live Updates: Counting underway for 28 seats across UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka
Article Text:
Counting also began at 8am for elections to five graduates’ and six teachers’ constituencies of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (File photo)

Karnataka MLC Election Results: BJP’s SV Sankanur takes early lead in West Graduates’ constituency

Bihar MLC Election Results: Congress candidate protests at Patna counting centre, alleges malpractice

Bihar MLC Election Results: Commotion over employee carrying files into counting hall

Maharashtra MLC Election Results: Mahayuti, MVA face test amid rebel candidates and internal differences

MLC Election Results 2026

: Bihar, UP await verdict in 19 Legislative Council Seats

Karnataka MLC Election Results:

UP MLC Election Results: Four-tier security cover at counting centre; 400 police personnel deployed

Bihar: 150 candidates contest eight MLC seats

Uttar Pradesh: Counting begins for 11 MLC seats

Maharashtra: 182 candidates in contest across five seats

Karnataka: Fourteen candidates in fray for MLC seat





The BJP has taken an early lead in the West Graduates’ Constituency election to the Karnataka Legislative Council, with its candidate, Prof SV Sankanur, maintaining a narrow advantage after the completion of the first round of counting.Around 14,000 votes are being counted in each round, with the counting process scheduled to be completed over six rounds.Cyclone Arnab' projected to cross Andhra Pradesh coast as 'very severe' cyclonic storm, IMD warns of winds up to 135 kmphCongress' Patna teachers constituency candidate Sanjay Yadav held a protest outside the counting centre at Bankipur school, alleging malpractices and the "absence of CCTV cameras" in the counting hall."Electoral malpractices have been reported. CCTV cameras have been installed outside the counting hall, but no device was placed inside the hall. It is an attempt to orchestrate malpractices," Yadav told news agency PTI.A commotion broke out at the Bankipur vote-counting centre in Patna after a government employee was spotted carrying a bundle of files into the counting hall.Counting was underway for the Patna Graduates’ and Patna Teachers’ constituencies of the Bihar Legislative Council.Reporters and supporters of candidates surrounded the employee as he made his way to the venue, questioning why the files were being taken into the counting hall.Police personnel deployed outside the counting centre intervened and asked the employee to place the bundle on the ground.Counting is underway for five Maharashtra Legislative Council constituencies on Tuesday, with the results expected to test the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance’s handling of internal dissent and the Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi’s (MVA) efforts to capitalise on differences within the ruling coalition.A total of 182 candidates are contesting across three graduates’ and two teachers’ constituencies, which together have 10,68,072 registered voters. Polling was held on October 23 across 2,419 polling stations, recording an overall turnout of around 72.96%.The contests have drawn attention amid rebel candidates, competing alliance interests and differences within both camps. The results will determine representatives for the five constituencies and offer an indication of the parties’ support among graduates and teachers.Counting is underway for 19 Legislative Council (MLC) seats across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, with graduate and teacher constituencies in focus.In Bihar, the contest covers eight seats — four graduate constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi, and four teacher constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran. The terms of eight sitting MLCs are due to end on November 16.The elections are being closely watched as a political test for the Congress government, with both the ruling party and the BJP-JD(S) alliance seeking to demonstrate their organisational strength among graduates and teachers. The results will also indicate how effectively the BJP and JD(S) have managed to transfer votes to each other's candidates under their alliance.Four-tier security arrangements have been put in place. Police personnel have been deployed in two shifts of 12 hours each for counting-related duties, with around 400 personnel assigned to each shift. In addition, an external drone team, mounted police and mobile squads have also been deployed as part of the security arrangements. Everyone is expected to ensure that the entire process is conducted in accordance with the Election Commission's guidelines. If police assistance is required at any point, the authorities should be informed immediately: SSP KaustubhVote counting for 28 Legislative Council seats across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka began on Tuesday. Polling for the seats was held on October 23.Security was tightened around the counting centre in Gorakhpur, with multiple layers of barricading and police personnel deployed to maintain order.In Uttar Pradesh, polling was held for 11 constituencies, including five Graduates' constituencies — Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut and Allahabad-Jhansi — and six Teachers' constituencies — Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut, Bareilly-Moradabad and Gorakhpur-Faizabad.In Maharashtra, 182 candidates are contesting five seats. The election covers three Graduates' constituencies — Pune, Nagpur and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar — and two Teachers' constituencies in Pune and Amravati.Karnataka is witnessing elections to four Legislative Council seats, covering 17 districts across the state. The key constituencies include Bengaluru and North-East Teachers' constituencies, along with the West and South-East Graduates' constituencies.In Bihar, polling was held for eight seats — four Graduates' constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi, and four Teachers' constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran.Counting began at 8am for the biennial elections to eight Bihar Legislative Council seats, with 90 candidates contesting four graduates’ constituencies and 60 in four teachers’ constituencies.Polling took place on October 23, recording a turnout of 82.85% in teachers’ constituencies and 53.42% in graduates’ seats. The four graduates’ constituencies — Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi — had 4.92 lakh eligible voters, while the four teachers’ constituencies — Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran — had 40,253 electors.Counting is being conducted at designated centres across the state. These include the Bankipur Government Girls’ Senior Secondary School in Patna, Khel Bhawan-cum-Vyayamshala Bhawan in Darbhanga, the MIT administrative block in Muzaffarpur for both Tirhut seats, and designated centres for the Kosi graduates’ and Saran teachers’ constituencies.The BJP has fielded candidates for four seats, while its ally JD(U) is contesting the remaining four. The Jan Suraaj Party, led by Prashant Kishor, is contesting all eight seats. The terms of the eight sitting MLCs expire on November 16.Counting also began at 8am for elections to five graduates’ and six teachers’ constituencies of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council.Chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa directed returning officers to ensure elaborate security arrangements and uninterrupted power supply at counting centres. Officials have been instructed to arrange automatic-switch generators, maintain CCTV surveillance and videography, restrict entry to authorised personnel and deploy trained counting staff.Additional personnel have been kept on reserve because Legislative Council elections use proportional representation through the single transferable vote system, which can make counting more time-consuming than conventional elections. Officials have also been directed to follow Election Commission guidelines and the Conduct of Elections Rules, with any negligence or procedural violations to be viewed seriously.In Maharashtra, counting began for five Legislative Council seats — three graduates’ and two teachers’ constituencies — involving 182 candidates. The constituencies had 10,68,072 registered voters and recorded an overall turnout of 72.96%.The contests are being closely watched for their implications for the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance and the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), particularly amid rebel candidates and competing alliance interests.In Nagpur, BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale is challenging sitting Congress MLC Abhijit Wanjarri. Pune graduates’ constituency has 47 candidates, including BJP nominee Smita Jadhav and NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) candidate Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav.In Pune teachers’ constituency, BJP nominee Kaustubh Gawde faces Congress MLC Jayant Asgaonkar, while Shiv Sena, led by Eknath Shinde, backs independent candidate Sachin Sanap. In Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, sitting MLC Satish Chavan faces NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil, while Amravati teachers’ constituency features sitting MLC Kiran Sarnaik against Congress nominee Aditi Pohare and several rebel candidates.Amravati recorded the highest turnout at 92.6%, followed by Pune teachers’ at 85.86%, Nagpur graduates’ at 64.84%, Pune graduates’ at 62.76% and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar graduates’ at 59.12%.With preferential voting in place, the final outcome could depend on subsequent preferences if no candidate reaches the required quota on first preferences alone.Counting of votes for the Karnataka Legislative Council’s West Graduates’ Constituency began on Tuesday at the University of Agricultural Sciences in Dharwad. As the election follows the preferential voting system, counting is expected to continue for several rounds, with the final result likely to be declared late in the evening or around midnight.The constituency, which covers Dharwad, Haveri, Gadag and Uttara Kannada districts, recorded a voter turnout of 75.6% in the October 23 election. Of the 97,400 registered voters, 73,658 cast their votes.A candidate needs to secure 50% plus one of the valid votes to win in the first round. Fourteen candidates are in the fray, including BJP’s SV Sankanur, who won the seat in 2014 and 2020, Congress candidate Mohan Limbikai and independent candidate Kanthkumar.Regional commissioner and returning officer KM Janaki said on Monday that votes would be counted across 14 tables. The Election Commission has appointed additional assistant returning officers to ensure the smooth conduct of the process. The strongroom is scheduled to be opened at 7.55am.
Article Summary: Counting is underway for 19 Legislative Council (MLC) seats across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, with graduate and teacher constituencies in focus. Polling was held on October 23 across 2,419 polling stations, recording an overall turnout of around 72.96%. The contests have drawn attention amid rebel candidates, competing alliance interests and differences within both camps.

Article Title: Delhi Police arrests 2 cops for extortion from drug peddler
Article Text: New Delhi: An alleged demand of Rs 2.5 lakh by a sub-inspector (SI) and a constable, extorted from a suspected drug peddler at Khajuri Khas police station, ended with both police officials being arrested. The peddler was reportedly held at the police station for over 24 hours, during which the peddler was allegedly threatened with jail time.According to police sources, the suspected peddler was arrested last week by the accused cops. Following his capture, the two police officers threatened to charge him under the stringent Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and send him to jail. Following discussions, they allegedly agreed to take Rs 2.5 lakh.The peddler was then made to withdraw money from an ATM. He reportedly gave Rs 1 lakh to the cops and his family was contacted to deliver the rest of the money. His relatives then registered a complaint at Timarpur police station, after which a trap was laid to catch them.The accused were asked to come to Timarpur to collect the remaining amount. When the two arrived, the constable was held while his accomplice ran away. Both were suspended after the incident.A case was registered under relevant sections of the BNS at Khajuri Khas police station against the two cops. Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: A suspected drug peddler was allegedly threatened with jail time by two police officers. The alleged demand of Rs 2.5 lakh by a sub-inspector (SI) and a constable led to their arrest. Both were suspended after the incident at Khajuri Khas police station.

Article Title: Delhi Schools, College Receive Hoax Bomb Threats; Police Search Premises
Article Text: New Delhi: Continuing a spate of hoax bomb threats targeting educational institutions in Delhi, three schools and a college received threatening emails Tuesday, prompting police to conduct searches of their premises.The first email was received at 11.22 am and the last at 12.35 pm, according to the Delhi Fire Services. Following the threats, Delhi Police deployed bomb disposal squads and sniffer dog units to carry out thorough searches of the premises. No suspicious object was found, and the threats were subsequently declared hoaxes.The incident comes days after a 16-year-old girl was apprehended for allegedly sending a bomb threat email to her school in southwest Delhi.
Article Summary: The first email was received at 11.22 am and the last at 12.35 pm. Delhi Police deployed bomb disposal squads and sniffer dog units to carry out thorough searches of the premises. No suspicious object was found, and the threats were subsequently declared hoaxes.

Article Title: Delhi high court declines to halt probe against woman journalist accused of casteist remarks against ACP at Jantar Mantar, seeks police response
Article Text:
Delhi high court has issued a notice regarding an FIR against a woman journalist for alleged misconduct





NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday refused to stay the investigation into a case registered against a woman journalist over alleged casteist remarks and public humiliation of a police officer during a protest near Jantar Mantar earlier this month.Justice Mini Pushkarna clarified that the court was neither rejecting the interim prayer at this stage nor passing any order on it, news agency PTI reported.The court issued notice to the Delhi Police and the assistant commissioner of police (ACP), who filed the complaint, on the journalist’s plea seeking quashing of the FIR. It asked them to file their replies before November 16, the next date of hearing.“I am not rejecting any prayer as of now. I am only issuing notice to them. The matter needs consideration; list for final hearing on November 16,” the judge said.Earlier, the woman journalist had filed a sexual assault complaint against the official. The Delhi Police Crime Branch is investigating her complaint, PTI reported.The journalist’s counsel argued that the FIR lodged by the ACP was intended to intimidate her and prevent her from pursuing the complaint against him.The high court passed a similar order on a separate plea by a male colleague of the journalist, who has also sought quashing of the FIR registered against him.The Delhi Police registered the FIR against the independent journalist and others based on an official’s complaint, PTI reported.The officer, who is posted at the Connaught Place sub-division of New Delhi district, alleged that casteist remarks, public humiliation and defamation were directed at him during the protest.The FIR invokes relevant provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Sections 221 (obstructing a public servant from discharging duty), 356(2) (defamation) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi high court refuses to stay investigation into a case registered against a woman journalist over alleged casteist remarks and public humiliation of a police officer. The court issued notice to the Delhi Police and the assistant commissioner of police (ACP), who filed the complaint, on the journalist’s plea seeking quashing of the FIR.

Article Title: Two arrested for possession of MD drug worth Rs 3 lakh
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Two individuals were arrested in Kolhapur for possession of a banned mephedrone (MD) drug, worth Rs3.09 lakh and weighing around 103g, which was seized by police.Upon receiving information, police from Jaysingpur division laid a trap at Chavare village in Hatkanangle tehsil on Sunday and stopped an SUV vehicle with no number plate, in which two individuals were carrying the drug, along with 10g ganja and a pistol with four live rounds. The cops also found glassware and glass tubes that are generally used to inhale the drug in vapourised form, a pocket electronic weighing scale and lighters.The arrested individuals have been identified as Ganesh Suresh Adekar (29), a resident of Ganeshnagar, Ichalkaranji, and Sad Munir Mulla (22) from Shivajinagar, Korochi. The third accused is from Nipani in Belagavi district of Karnataka. All three have been booked under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and Arms Act at Peth Vadgaon police station.The police are investigating from where the drug was sourced by the accused. The cops suspect that the two arrested individuals were out to sell the MD drug. “The court has given us the custody of the accused for five days. We will dig deeper into the racket and investigate links related to the drug trade,” said Gorakh Choudhar, police inspector of Peth Vadgaon police station.
Article Summary: Two individuals were arrested in Kolhapur for possession of a banned mephedrone (MD) drug, worth Rs3.09 lakh and weighing around 103g. The arrested individuals have been identified as Ganesh Suresh Adekar (29), a resident of Ganeshnagar, Ichalkaranji, and Sad Munir Mulla (22) from Shivajinagar, Korochi.

Article Title: AICC member Khodaniya appeals Kolhapur residents to join Nov 1 Ramlila rally
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





All India Congress Committee (AICC) member and former Rajasthan minister Dinesh Khodaniya has appealed to Kolhapur residents to join the “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao” rally at New Delhi ’s Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1, to be led by leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi Addressing a news conference at the Congress office in Kolhapur, Khodaniya alleged that names of crores of voters had been deleted from electoral rolls across the country during the Election Commission of India ’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.He said Congress workers were trying to get the names of affected voters restored to the rolls and accused the BJP of weakening democracy. “We will continue our protests to demand that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar accept responsibility and resign,” Khodaniya said.Opposition parties will demand the return of ballot papers and an end to electronic voting machine use in Indian elections. “With the help of the deletions and use of EVMs, the BJP has won several elections. The people are against the BJP and it should be genuinely reflected in the voting results. Congress will keep building the heat to get reforms done in the election system,” said Khodaniya.
Article Summary: Former Rajasthan minister Dinesh Khodaniya has appealed to Kolhapur residents to join the “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally at New Delhi ’s Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1. The rally will be led by leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: MK Stalin urges President Droupadi Murmu to seek action against CEC over SIR, 97 lakh voter deletions
Article Text:
DMK president MK Stalin has requested President Droupadi Murmu to intervene in the electoral roll controversy.





CHENNAI: DMK president MK Stalin has urged President Droupadi Murmu to intervene in the ongoing controversy over the revision of electoral rolls and seek parliamentary and judicial action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In a memorandum dated Oct 26, Stalin alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls had resulted in the deletion of a large number of genuine voters in Tamil Nadu and accused the chief election commissioner of taking unilateral and unconstitutional decisions by overriding the views of the other two election commissioners.“The DMK president’s memorandum was sent by e-mail as an appointment from the President was not forthcoming for a DMK delegation till Wednesday,” said a source.Stalin sought a reference to Parliament under Article 86(2) of the Constitution for initiating necessary action against the CEC.He also urged the President to refer to the Supreme Court, under Article 143, the question of the validity of the deletion of 97 lakh electors from Tamil Nadu’s rolls during the SIR exercise.The DMK leader sought a direction to the ECI that the “tainted post-SIR roll” not be used for any future election or by-election and that the pre-SIR roll be restored.
Article Summary: DMK president MK Stalin has requested President Droupadi Murmu to intervene in the electoral roll controversy. Stalin alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls had resulted in the deletion of a large number of genuine voters in Tamil Nadu.

Article Title: Properties of former TN minister Anbil Mahesh should be seized, BJP leader demands
Article Text:
Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi





COIMBATORE: BJP state general secretary A P Muruganandam has demanded a thorough probe into an alleged Rs 100crore corruption case involving former Tamil Nadu school education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi and called for the seizure of assets accumulated in the names of Mahesh and his alleged benamis.In a statement on Tuesday, Muruganandam alleged that corruption in the school education department had brought disrepute to the state. He said it involved issuing new licences and renewing recognition for private schools in exchange of bribes.Muruganandam said private schools should meet safety and infrastructure norms, including structurally sound buildings, fire safety measures, proper ventilation and playground facilities. He alleged that approvals were granted to ineligible schools for bribes, risking the safety of students.He added that private schools passed on bribery costs to parents through fees and other charges. He called the alleged Rs 100 crore corruption exploitation of poor and middle-class families. He asked whether such a large-scale scam could have occurred without the knowledge or involvement of senior political leaders, IAS officers and intermediaries.Muruganandam sought referral of the case to the Enforcement Directorate and other central agencies to investigate the alleged movement of illegal funds.
Article Summary: BJP state general secretary A P Muruganandam has demanded a thorough probe into an alleged Rs 100crore corruption case. He called for the seizure of assets accumulated in the names of Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi and his alleged benamis.

Article Title: Man held for murdering homosexual partner in Tirupur
Article Text:
Tirupur

:





A textile worker was arrested for murdering his homosexual partner by hitting him on the head with a grinding stone at a rented room in Chamundipuram on Saturday.Police said the deceased Muthu , 26, and the accused Chinnaram, 21, both from Madurai district, were working at a private knitwear unit and living together on the terrace of an apartment building near Chamundipuram.The crime came to light on Sunday, when neighbours found Muthu dead inside the room. 15 Velampalayam police who were alerted, recovered the body and sent it to Tirupur Govt Hospital for a postmortem.Police launched a search for Chinnaram, who was missing from the room. Meanwhile, Chinnaram surrendered at Usilampatti police station in Madurai district on Sunday, after which a Tirupur police team secured him and brought him to Tirupur for interrogation.“During questioning, he revealed that the two had been living together for about six years. An argument broke out on Saturday night after Muthu’s family began looking for a bride for him. Chinnaram objected to the marriage plans, and the quarrel escalated, following which he allegedly used a grinding stone to assault Muthu, killing him,” said a police officer.Meanwhile, police also scotched rumours that the murder was linked to alleged threats involving a video. “No such video was found on either of their mobile phones,” the officer added.A case has been registered and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A textile worker was arrested for murdering his homosexual partner by hitting him on the head with a grinding stone at a rented room in Chamundipuram. Police said the deceased Muthu, 26, and the accused Chinnaram, 21, both from Madurai district, were working at a private knitwear unit and living together.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Husband slashes wife outside court during divorce hearing in Kanyakumari district
Article Text:
Madurai:





A woman appearing for a divorce hearing was critically injured after her estranged husband attacked her with a sickle outside the Padmanabhapuram family court in Kanyakumari district on Tuesday.Jerlin Prema, 32, was walking towards the court with her younger brother, Jerin, when Vincent Raj, a mason from Eethavilai near Thuckalay, intercepted her near the entrance and repeatedly slashed her with a concealed sickle.Lawyers who intervened were threatened with the weapon. Raj fled, but advocates and members of the public chased him for about 150m, caught him on Palace Road and handed him over to Thuckalay police.Prema, who suffered injuries to her head and limbs, was taken to Thuckalay govt hospital before being referred to Government Medical College Hospital in Asaripallam, where she was admitted for intensive treatment. Later, she was moved to a private hospital.Prema, who worked at a shop, married Raj about eight years ago. The couple have a son. Following marital disputes, she moved to her parents’ home in Ponmanai and filed for divorce. Police sources alleged that Raj had frequently assaulted her.Police registered a case of attempted murder and arrested Raj. Investigators said other criminal cases were pending against him.
Article Summary: Jerlin Prema, 32, was walking towards the court with her younger brother, Jerin. Vincent Raj, a mason from Eethavilai near Thuckalay, intercepted her near the entrance and repeatedly slashed her with a concealed sickle.

Article Title: Robbery accused who bit Kochi resident held in West Bengal
Article Text:
Kochi

:

Man held with drugs:

Man gets 15 years’ RI:





A 42-year-old man was arrested in connection with a robbery attempt in which he allegedly bit off the finger of a resident while trying to escape. He was arrested in West Bengal on Tuesday.The accused Biffia Urao, 42, of Chiktu Jota, Ketagabur, Darjeeling , had been absconding after the incident.A case was registered at the Eloor police station under sections 309(5), 126(2), 118(2) and 115(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.The police examined call detail records and other information and learned that the accused was in West Bengal. Based on the direction of Kalamassery inspector A L Abhilash, a team led by Eloor station house officer Sachin Lal reached the Naxalbari police station limits and took Urao into custody.The accused was formally arrested, produced before the Kalamassery judicial first-class magistrate court and remanded in judicial custody.A 39-year-old man was arrested with MDMA and Rs 5 lakh cash as part of Operation Toofan in Kochi city on Monday night.The accused is Anson Antony of Elamakkara. Police seized 30.43g of MDMA, 10.8g of ganja and 1.4g of hashish from the house where he was staying on Puthukkalavattam Parayil Road, within the limits of the Elamakkara police station.Police said the seized cash was allegedly earned through the sale of MDMA.A man has been sentenced to 15 years’ rigorous imprisonment and fined Rs 35,000 for sexually assaulting a woman with physical and intellectual disabilities.The accused is Joshi, 36, of Mundamveli Colony, Thoppumpady.The incident took place on Nov 16, 2020, at the accused’s house.Thoppumpady police registered an FIR under Sections 450 and 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code and filed a chargesheet after completing the investigation.
Article Summary: A 42-year-old man was arrested in connection with a robbery attempt in which he allegedly bit off the finger of a resident while trying to escape. The accused Biffia Urao, 42, of Chiktu Jota, Ketagabur, Darjeeling, had been absconding after the incident.
